title: A Mat Beside the Field
bigQuestion: Why do wrestling, boxing, fencing and judo each need a room of their own?

story.title: A Jacket Beside a Ball Bag
story.kicker: A folded white jacket hangs in a school hallway next to a bag of baseballs.
paragraphs: Two hooks hang by the gym door. A bag of baseballs sits on one hook. A folded white jacket and a belt hang on the other.
Sam touches the jacket. The cloth is thick and rough. "That is for the judo club," says Ms. Park. "Judo began at a school in Tokyo, Japan, in 1882."
"Where do they play?" asks Sam. "Not on the grass," says Ms. Park. "Judo uses a soft mat. Baseball uses a diamond. Each game has its own room."
Sam looks from the jacket to the ball bag. Two clubs share one hallway. They go to two very different floors. One floor is soft. One is grass and dirt.
story.think: Why might a judo club and a baseball team need different floors?

lessons.title: Wrestlers on a Tomb Wall
lessons.mainIdea: Painters in old Egypt showed hundreds of pairs of wrestlers on tomb walls about 4,000 years ago.
reading: Beni Hasan is a place along the Nile River in Egypt. Leaders were buried there in *tombs* cut into cliffs. The tombs are about 4,000 years old.
Painters covered some tomb walls with wrestlers. One wall shows hundreds of pairs, one after another. Each pair is painted in a different pose.
The paintings tell us wrestling is very, very old. Egyptians watched it long before soccer had rules.

words.d: a room or grave where a person is buried

look.title: A painted wall
look.text: Picture a cool room cut into a cliff in Egypt. The wall is covered with small painted people. Two by two, they wrestle in rows, like a long comic strip.
look.prompt: What can a painting on a wall teach us about people long ago?

check.why: They are painted in tombs at Beni Hasan, Egypt.

check.q: About how old are the Beni Hasan tombs?
check.why: The tombs were made about 4,000 years ago.

check.q: What does one tomb wall show?
check.why: One wall shows hundreds of pairs of wrestlers.

lessons.title: A Wrestling School in Greece
lessons.mainIdea: Old Greeks built wrestling schools, and wrestling has been in the modern Olympics since 1896.
reading: Old Greeks trained in a building called a *palaestra*. It had an open yard with rooms around it. Wrestlers practiced there.
By tradition, wrestling joined the old Olympic Games at Olympia in 708 BCE. The modern Olympics began in Athens in 1896. Wrestling was there, too.
For a long time, only men wrestled at the Olympics. Women's wrestling was first held at the Athens Games in 2004.

words.d: an old Greek building where wrestlers trained

look.title: A yard with rooms
look.text: Picture an open yard in old Greece. Rooms with columns stand all around it. Young men train in the yard. A teacher watches from the shade.
look.prompt: How is this old training place like a school gym today?

check.q: What was a palaestra?
check.why: A palaestra was a Greek building where wrestlers trained.

check.q: When did the modern Olympics begin?
check.why: The modern Olympics began in Athens in 1896.

check.q: When was women's Olympic wrestling first held?
check.why: Women first wrestled at the Athens Games in 2004.

sections.title: A Square, a Strip, a Circle

lessons.title: A Roped Square
lessons.mainIdea: Boxing's Queensberry Rules of 1867 called for gloves and a square ring.
reading: In 1867, new boxing rules were printed in England. They were named for the Marquess of Queensberry. They are called the *Queensberry Rules*.
The rules called for padded gloves and rounds of three minutes. Matches were held in a *ring*. A boxing ring is really a square with ropes around it.
Boxing joined the Olympics in St. Louis in 1904. Women first boxed at the Olympics in London in 2012.

words.d: boxing rules printed in England in 1867
the roped square where boxing matches are held

look.title: The first rule
look.text: The first rule says a match should be a fair stand-up boxing match in a ring 24 feet across, or as close to that size as possible.
look.prompt: What does the first rule tell you about the room for boxing?

check.q: What shape is a boxing ring?

check.why: Women first boxed at the London Olympics in 2012.

lessons.title: A Long Thin Strip
lessons.mainIdea: Fencing uses a long, narrow floor called a strip, and it has been in every modern Olympics.
reading: Fencing is a sport with thin, blunt swords. Fencers stay on a long, narrow floor. It is called a *strip*, or a piste.
A strip is 14 meters long. That is longer than a school bus. It is less than 2 meters wide.
Fencing has been in every modern Olympics since 1896. Women first fenced at the Olympics in Paris in 1924.

words.d: the long, narrow floor used for fencing; also called a piste

lessons.title: A Clay Circle in Japan
lessons.mainIdea: Sumo wrestlers in Japan meet in a round clay ring called a dohyo.
reading: *Sumo* is a very old kind of wrestling from Japan. Sumo wrestlers meet in a round ring called a *dohyo*. It is made of packed clay.
Straw bales mark the edge of the circle. Before a bout, wrestlers toss salt into the ring. In Shinto tradition, salt makes a place clean.
Pro sumo holds six big tournaments each year. In pro sumo, only men may enter the ring. Women and girls wrestle in amateur sumo.

words.d: a very old kind of wrestling from Japan
the round clay ring used in sumo

lessons.title: A School Called the Kodokan
lessons.mainIdea: Kano Jigoro started judo at the Kodokan school in Tokyo in 1882.
reading: *Kano* Jigoro was a teacher in Japan. In 1882 he opened a school in Tokyo. It was called the Kodokan. It began in a small room at a Buddhist temple.
Kano named his art *judo*. The name means "gentle way." Students trained on straw mats called tatami. They wore thick cotton jackets.
A judo room is called a dojo. In many judo schools, students bow as they step onto the mat. They see the bow as a sign of respect.

words.d: Kano Jigoro, the teacher who started judo in Tokyo in 1882
a Japanese art whose name means gentle way
a training room for judo and other Japanese arts

lessons.title: From Tokyo to the Olympics
lessons.mainIdea: Judo joined the Olympics when Tokyo held the Games in 1964.
reading: In 1909, Kano became the first person from Asia on the *International Olympic Committee*. That group runs the Olympic Games.
Tokyo held the Olympics in 1964. Judo joined the Games that year. Men were the only judo players at first.
Women's judo became an Olympic medal sport in Barcelona in 1992. Taekwondo, from Korea, joined in 2000.

words.d: the group that runs the Olympic Games

lessons.title: Wrestling Mats in Illinois
lessons.mainIdea: Illinois high schools held a boys wrestling state meet in 1937 and a girls state meet in 2022.
reading: The Illinois High School Association, or *IHSA*, began in 1900. It runs state contests for Illinois high schools.
School wrestlers meet on a thick, padded *mat*. The first IHSA boys state champions came in 1937.
Girls wrestled in Illinois before they had their own meet. Their first IHSA state finals came in 2022.

words.d: the Illinois High School Association, begun in 1900
the thick, padded floor used for wrestling
